Approximate inference requires a declared target measure, persistent parameters, support-covering proposals and diagnostics beyond particle weights. Threshold bounds require control near the boundary, and temporal transport requires adapted information. The repaired finite coupling supplies explicit initial and common-loss premises; feedback can amplify local errors.
